findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext within the EC2 user_data script, exposing sensitive credentials to anyone with access to instance metadata, the Terraform state, or the console.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, leaving data at rest unencrypted and vulnerable to exposure if the underlying storage is compromised.
The EBS snapshot inherits from an unencrypted volume and has no encryption configured, exposing data at rest in the snapshot.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, permitting anyone on the internet to attempt to connect via SSH, greatly increasing attack surface.

The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 with no additional restriction, exposing the web service broadly (though this may be intended for a public web server, it still increases exposure surface in combination with other findings).
The subnet has map_public_ip_on_launch set to true, causing instances launched in it to automatically receive public IP addresses, increasing exposure to direct internet access.
The subnet has map_public_ip_on_launch set to true, causing instances launched in it to automatically receive public IP addresses, increasing exposure to direct internet access.

findings.issue_category: missing bucket encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket used for storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block/ACL restrictions defined, risking exposure of sensitive network traffic logs.
